subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in normal success-path mode that resets a session immediately after a successful agentic memory flush instead of running compaction, and what config, consent, timeout, audit, provider-routing, and security boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining behavior changes session lifecycle, silent tool-capable memory execution, provider/model selection, and privacy/security semantics, so automation should not choose the product policy alone.

options.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
options.body: Approve an explicit opt-in mode with duplicate-reset protection, timeout/cancellation handling, durable-memory expectations, user or audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Fold into reset-memory policy
options.body: Track the remaining behavior under the open reset-memory lifecycle issue so reset-time and compaction-threshold memory preservation share one contract.

options.title: Keep compaction as the supported path
options.body: Decline automatic reset-after-flush and keep current model overrides plus compaction/exhaustion recovery as the supported cost-control behavior.

recommendation.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit opt-in mode with duplicate-reset protection, timeout/cancellation handling, durable-memory expectations, user or audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to both the pre-compaction memory flush primitive and the /new reset behavior that the remaining feature would combine.
